# SSH-014: Authorized keys are strong and not stale

- **Group:** SSH
- **Severity when it fails:** moderate
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

DSA keys and RSA keys under 2048 bits are weak enough to retire. Keys in root's authorized_keys while root login is off are leftovers that start working again the day someone relaxes PermitRootLogin. Only the key type, size and SHA256 fingerprint (as ssh-keygen -l prints it) are kept, never the key or its comment; stackward diff compares fingerprints to report a new authorized key.

## Verify by hand

```sh
ssh-keygen -lf ~USER/.ssh/authorized_keys
```

## How to fix it

Replace weak keys with ed25519 (ssh-keygen -t ed25519) and remove root's authorized keys once nothing logs in as root.

Run `stackward explain SSH-014` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
